changes.why: The pooled relative risks carry the report's safety claims (reactogenicity, SAEs) on which half of the evidence summary and the recommendation rest, so their role is primary rather than ancillary.

equity.level_reason: Age (adults aged ≥60 years) only defines the population. Long-term care residence and frailty appear as clinical risk factors and in a trial-enrollment limitation, which does not raise the level.

level_alternative.reason: Older adults in long-term care facilities could be read as a congregate-setting social position, and the Evidence to Recommendation review names equity, so equity would be raised only as a limitation.

ev.q: for use in adults aged ≥60 years
the numbers of persons enrolled in the trials who were frail, were of advanced age, and lived in long-term care facilities were limited

equity.equity_measurement: No social-position dimension is reported for trial participants; frail, advanced-age and long-term care residents were under-enrolled and immunocompromised persons excluded.

notes: data_focus 'yes' kept: beyond citing trial VE, the Work Group's systematic review reports its own pooled RRs. GRADE and the multiplicity-adjusted CIs (96.95%, 97.5%) are evidence-rating and inference details, not separate procedures.
